description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by enrollment level, sex, and race/ethnicity for undergraduate and graduate students. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYLEV, with total counts for men and women and counts for all nine race/ethnicity categories.

12-month instructional activity measured in total credit hours and/or contact hours, reported for undergraduate and graduate activity. The table supports 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment measures and is distinct from the headcount table; no further row-level key is specified in the description.

Institution-level academic library data for 2005-06, including library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services; this table contains only the subset of survey variables consistent with the library information later collected in IPEDS. It applies only to degree-granting institutions, and expenditure data are available only for degree-granting institutions with total expenditures over $100,000.

Awards conferred from July 1, 2005 through June 30, 2006, broken down by six-digit CIP program, award level, first or second major, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL; the table reports total awards plus counts for men and women overall and within each of nine race/ethnicity categories. It contains multiple records per institution and covers certificate and degree awards.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and attendance status and student level (EFLEVEL).

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and attendance status and student level (EFALEVEL).

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY). Enrollment by age is optional in even-numbered years, so 2006 (even) has age data only from institutions that reported this optional component.

Counts of first-time freshmen broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school in the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID) and state of residence (EFCSTATE). Enrollment by residence is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2006 (even) is not an optional residence-reporting year and this table has the scheduled residence data.

Fall enrollment counts in selected major fields—Education, Engineering, Biological/Life Sciences, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, Business, Law, Dentistry, and Medicine—broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. This table is limited to 4-year institutions; each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS ID (UNITID), major field, attendance status, and student level (EFCIPLEV).

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, applicable only to institutions with undergraduate students. Only academic-year institutions report entering-class data; institutions with less-than-one-year programs do not have retention data. Retention was first collected in 2006 as rates only, without the underlying counts, and retention data describe students beginning in fall 2005 and persisting or completing in fall 2006.

Institution-level revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards. The row grain is one primary institution identified by its institution ID; this is the main GASB institutional-finance table, distinct from the separate component-unit tables.

Assets, liabilities, and net assets for component units of public GASB institutions that use FASB accounting standards. Each record is identified by the primary institution and component unit, including the component unit’s name and general nature; component-unit financial data are available for fiscal years 2002 through 2007.

Assets, liabilities, and net assets for component units of public GASB institutions that use GASB accounting standards. Each record is identified by the primary institution and component unit, including the component unit’s name and general nature; component-unit financial data are available for fiscal years 2002 through 2007.

Institution-level revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for all private not-for-profit institutions and for public institutions that use FASB accounting standards. The row grain is one reporting institution identified by its institution ID, combining these two FASB-using institution groups rather than public GASB institutions.

Institution-level revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards. The row grain is one private for-profit reporting institution identified by its institution ID, with expenditures reported by category rather than the function-and-natural-classification detail used in the other institutional finance forms.

Graduation and transfer outcomes for full-time, first-time undergraduates at four-year and two-year institutions, including bachelor’s-degree seekers and other degree/certificate seekers at four-year institutions. Records are uniquely defined by IPEDS ID (UNITID), cohort and graduation status (GRTYPE), with counts broken down by gender and race/ethnicity; the four-year cohort entered in 2000 and the two-year cohort entered in 2003, and outcomes include completion within 150% of normal time plus more detailed bachelor’s completion milestones and transfers out.

Graduation completion and transfer outcomes for the 2003 cohort of full-time, first-time degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions. The table contains institution-level counts enrolled, completing within 150% of normal time, or transferring out.

Fall staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, and faculty or tenure status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPRECTP, which combines occupational category, tenure status, and employment status.

Fall staff counts broken down by occupational category, full- or part-time status, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SABDTYPE, which defines occupational category and full- or part-time status. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2006 (even) has incomplete data for many institutions.

Fall employee counts broken down by primary function or occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SCNLEVEL; it applies to degree-granting institutions with fewer than 15 full-time employees, all nondegree-granting institutions, and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2006 (even) has incomplete data for many institutions.

Fall full-time instruction, research, and public-service staff counts broken down by faculty or tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK, which combines faculty status and academic rank; it applies only to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2006 (even) has incomplete data for many institutions.

Fall full-time new-hire counts broken down by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SGTYPE, which defines the primary occupation; it applies only to degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2006 (even) has incomplete data for many institutions.

Full-time nonmedical instructional staff counts and salary outlays broken down by gender, academic rank, and contract length. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID, ARANK, and CONTRACT; contract categories include 9/10-month, 11/12-month, and equated 9/10-month contracts.
Counts of full-time nonmedical instructional faculty with contracts shorter than 9 months, broken down by academic rank. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK.

Full-time nonmedical instructional staff receiving fringe benefits, with total and average benefit expenditures, broken down by contract length and benefit-plan type. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and BENTYPE.

Full-time nonmedical instructional staff counts in 4-year institutions broken down by faculty status, contract length, gender, and academic rank. Each row is identified by UNITID, CONTRACT, and ARANK; faculty status includes tenured, tenure-track, not-on-tenure-track or no-tenure-system, and without-faculty-status categories.

Survey-component response status records identified by institution and survey component, including response, imputation, applicability, parent/child reporting, and revised-submission indicators. The row grain is institution × survey component.

Directory information records for each institution, including names and addresses, URLs, active status, Title IV participation, control and level, highest award offered, and Carnegie classifications. The row grain is one institution.

Institution-level records of educational offerings and award levels, control and affiliations, special learning opportunities, organization, admissions, and athletic associations. Admissions, applicants, and test-score fields apply only to institutions without an open-admissions policy; the row grain is one institution.

Student charges for full academic-year programs, including tuition and required fees for full-time undergraduate and graduate students, per-credit-hour charges for part-time undergraduate and graduate students, first-professional charges, and published price of attendance for full-time first-time undergraduates. This table applies to institutions whose primarily academic, credit-hour programs use a semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic-year calendar; the row grain is one institution.

Student charges by vocational or occupational program, including the number of programs, price of attendance for entering students in the largest program, and tuition, fees, and books-and-supplies charges for up to five additional programs. This applies to institutions using clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs; records are identified by institution and program position, such as largest or additional program.
Institutional mission statements or links to those statements. The row grain is one institution.

Institution-level student financial aid data for the July 1, 2005–June 30, 2006 award year, reported annually for eligible institutions. The table covers only full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students; each record is defined by institution and aid source/type, with the number of recipients and average dollar amount received. Aid categories include federal grants, state/local grants, institutional grants, and student loans.
